headline_seed: Patrick Stewart, legendary actor of ‘Star Trek’ and ‘X-Men’ fame, dies at 86 - AP News

consensus_facts: Patrick Stewart, the British actor, died at age 86.
He died on Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles.
His death followed 'a brief and poignant journey' with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, per a statement from spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak.
He was best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in the 'Star Trek' franchise and Professor Charles Xavier in the 'X-Men' franchise.
He played Picard across 'Star Trek: The Next Generation' (seven seasons), four feature films, and three seasons of the Paramount+ series 'Star Trek: Picard.'
He was set to reprise the role of Professor X in 'Avengers: Doomsday,' scheduled for release in December 2026.
He joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966 and had a decades-long classical stage career on Broadway and London's West End.
He was born in Mirfield/Yorkshire, England, in 1940.
He is survived by his wife Sunny (Ozell) and two children, Daniel and Sophie/Sophia.
He was nominated for a Tony Award in 2008 for his Broadway performance in 'Macbeth.'
Marvel Studios released a statement calling him a 'singular talent,' 'generous collaborator,' and 'true gentleman' who defined Xavier for generations of fans.
'X-Men' co-star Hugh Jackman paid tribute, calling him 'one of the greats of stage and screen' and 'a tremendous friend and man.'
'Star Trek' co-star William Shatner paid tribute, saying Stewart brought 'intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did.'
His spokesperson's statement said he was 'held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter' and praised his 'invincible grace.'

positions.Associated Press: Refers to his older brother Trevor and mentions children Daniel and Sophia; AP memoir section uses 'Sophia'

positions.BBC News: Attributes the announcement to a post on Stewart's Instagram
positions.ABC News: Attributes it to a statement shared on his social media by spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak

framing_analysis.Associated Press: Deepest, most writerly obituary in the dossier. Leads on 'Shakespearean gravitas' and emphasizes that Stewart spent more of his career onstage than on screen. Uniquely surfaces biographical hardship: his working-class Yorkshire upbringing without an indoor toilet, his father's domestic violence against his mother, and Stewart's resulting patronage of the charity Refuge. Heavy on his Macbeth, RSC tenure, and memoir 'Making It So.' Treats the franchise fame as secondary to the stage legacy.
framing_analysis.CBS News: Comprehensive and list-oriented. Leads with 'legendary' and franchise roles, then pivots to an unusually complete career catalogue: three Olivier Awards, Tony nomination, Grammy (1995 Best Spoken Word Album for Children), OBE (2001) and knighthood (2010), his three marriages, voice work on 'Family Guy' and 'American Dad,' and advocacy causes (social justice, women's rights, domestic abuse, veterans, refugees, animal rights). Most tribute-heavy outlet, including a lengthy Seth MacFarlane quote. Emphasizes breadth of his body of work.
framing_analysis.BBC News: Frames him through a British and Yorkshire lens. Uniquely foregrounds his lifelong support of Huddersfield Town football club and their 'Terrier' tribute, and the knighthood anecdote crediting his English teacher. Attributes the death announcement to his Instagram. Notes the Hollywood Walk of Fame star and flowers to be placed in tribute. Shorter, hometown-pride framing distinct from the American obituaries.
framing_analysis.Los Angeles Times: Leads on the 'Shakespearean actor turned Star Trek captain' arc. Emphasizes the 'unknown British Shakespearean actor' casting anecdote and his own retelling of it (the Brent Spiner trailer sign), drawing on prior LAT interviews. Focuses heavily on the Marvel/X-Men lineage through 'Logan' and 'Avengers: Doomsday' and reprints the full Marvel Studios statement. Omits the domestic-abuse backstory and awards catalogue.
framing_analysis.The New York Times: Headline-only in this dossier ('7 Memorable Patrick Stewart Performances'). No body text retrievable, so no framing can be assessed beyond that NYT chose a curated-performances angle rather than a straight obituary.
framing_analysis.NBC News: Standard obituary framing leading on 'beloved' and the two iconic roles. Notable for the garbled page scrape stuffing in unrelated 'For Subscribers' political headlines. Uniquely specifies 'Avengers: Doomsday' as the 'eighth time' reprising Xavier and notes his most recent work: voice-over in 'The Sheep Detectives' and the Prime Video series 'Bait' (both 2026). Mentions his 1971 Broadway debut in 'A Midsummer Night's Dream.'
framing_analysis.ABC News: Shortest and most news-wire/developing-story in tone. Leads on the 'brief battle' with Alzheimer's and Lewy body dementia and devotes unusual space to explaining what those diseases are, citing the CDC. Explicitly flags 'It is unclear when Stewart was diagnosed' and labels the piece 'a developing story.' Light on career detail and tributes.

primary_source_alignment: No primary source document was located for this story. The underlying primary text is the family/spokesperson statement from Kelly Bush Novak, which is quoted (in overlapping fragments) by AP, CBS, BBC, LA Times, NBC, and ABC. The quoted language — 'a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,' 'warm embrace of family and friends,' 'invincible grace' — is consistent across the outlets that reproduce it, suggesting faithful transcription of a single shared statement rather than independent reporting.
Because multiple outlets draw the same quotes from the same statement, corroboration here reflects a common source, not independent verification.
missing_context: No outlet reports when Stewart was diagnosed with Alzheimer's or Lewy body dementia; ABC News explicitly flags this as unclear and the AP notes the diagnoses 'had not been previously disclosed.'
The exact spelling of his daughter's name is inconsistent across outlets (Sophie vs. Sophia); no outlet reconciles it.

No outlet states a precise cause or time of death beyond 'Wednesday' and the disease context; the announcement itself came Thursday, Oct. 29/30, creating minor date ambiguity between the 'died Wednesday' framing and the Thursday statement.
The claim that 'Avengers: Doomsday' marks his 'eighth' Xavier appearance (NBC) is not corroborated or itemized by other outlets, which give vaguer counts.
No outlet provides official confirmation of the diagnoses from a medical authority — all rely solely on the spokesperson/family statement.

Several outlets rely on the same spokesperson statement and the same social-media tributes (Jackman, Shatner, Marvel), so apparent cross-outlet agreement partly reflects shared sourcing rather than independent confirmation.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Six outlets independently confirm the same core facts (who, when, how, the signature roles, the survivors) with no material factual conflict — divergences are limited to emphasis (stage legacy vs. franchise fame vs. Yorkshire pride) and trivial details like a name spelling. This is a well-corroborated obituary suited to a straightforward REPORT rather than a coverage-divergence META.
